desc: Build brute-force verifier (stack enumeration + O(N²) interval DP) for small N and establish ground truth on random tests.

Run harness; test hypotheses against brute force: (a) stack-process bijection [CONFIRMED], (b) prefix-DP decomposition bestFull(j+1,i-1) = f[i-1] − f[j] [REFUTED], (c) sorted-order extreme pairing [REFUTED]; collect counterexamples.

Derive the key structural insight for O(N log N): prove that in the stack-based DP, the optimal stack content can be represented as a Pareto frontier of (score, top_value) pairs per depth, and that dominance can be decided by comparing score ± value; implement a segment-tree DP over positions where each node stores the best achievable score for pairing with a future element, enabling O(N log N) transitions.
Validate the derived fast recurrence against brute force / interval DP on many random small cases and edge cases (all equal, N=2, monotone arrays, odd N with leftover choice).
Handle parity (N odd → exactly one leftover) and 64-bit arithmetic.
Implement final O(N log N)/O(N) Python solution reading stdin, writing stdout, enclosed in required delimiters.
